evidence.claim: The Federal Government has control and command of the Armed Forces.
evidence.title: Chapter 2: Armed Forces
evidence.publisher: pakistani.org (text of the Constitution of Pakistan)
evidence.excerpt: The Federal Government has control and command of the Armed Forces.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct constitutional text on state command authority.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows the formal state command structure under Sharif's government, but not a target-period nuclear decision by Sharif personally.
contrary_evidence: This general command clause does not by itself show day-to-day nuclear command or how much practical autonomy the military retained.

evidence.claim: India said it was reviewing procedures after accidentally firing a missile into Pakistan during routine maintenance.
evidence.title: India says reviewing procedures after missile accidentally fired into Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: India said it was reviewing procedures after accidentally firing a missile into Pakistan during routine maintenance.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting is a strong independent corroborator of the incident context.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period, corroborating the March 2022 crisis context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context only; the incident originated in India, not from Sharif's own action.
contrary_evidence: This does not show Sharif's conduct directly, only the external crisis he had to manage.

evidence.claim: Shehbaz Sharif wrote to Narendra Modi seeking meaningful dialogue, peaceful and cooperative ties, and regional peace and security; he also framed Kashmir resolution as part of that settlement.
evidence.title: Seek meaningful talks with India, peaceful ties: Shehbaz Sharif to PM Modi
evidence.excerpt: Shehbaz Sharif wrote to Narendra Modi seeking meaningful dialogue, peaceful and cooperative ties, and regional peace and security; he also framed Kashmir resolution as part of that settlement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent mainstream reporting quotes the letter and Sharif's own tweet from the same exchange.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period after Sharif took office in April 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct Sharif statement; strong personal attribution.
contrary_evidence: This is diplomatic rhetoric and does not by itself prove durable policy change or concessions.

evidence.claim: Pakistan said cross-border attacks from Afghanistan had risen, asked Kabul to secure the border, condemned militant use of Afghan soil, and reaffirmed respect for Afghan sovereignty.
evidence.title: PRESS RELEASE
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan said cross-border attacks from Afghanistan had risen, asked Kabul to secure the border, condemned militant use of Afghan soil, and reaffirmed respect for Afghan sovereignty.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated official government statement with concrete border-security claims and a de-escalatory closing line.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in-period and immediately after Sharif took office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government attribution is strong, but this is the foreign ministry's line rather than a personal PM directive.
contrary_evidence: Afghan authorities denied the accusations, so the statement is one-sided and not a neutral finding.

evidence.claim: Pakistan said its forces were being targeted from Afghanistan and the incident followed purported Pakistani air strikes inside Afghan airspace; UNAMA voiced concern about reported civilian casualties.
evidence.title: Pakistan says cross-border attacks from Afghanistan have increased
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan said its forces were being targeted from Afghanistan and the incident followed purported Pakistani air strikes inside Afghan airspace; UNAMA voiced concern about reported civilian casualties.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters is a strong independent source; the piece also records UNAMA concern, which adds corroborating monitoring context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: This is government border-policy context under Sharif; the report does not prove Sharif personally ordered the alleged strikes.
contrary_evidence: The article does not independently verify the alleged Pakistani air strikes, and Pakistan denied carrying them out.

evidence.claim: The Taliban in Afghanistan mediated a temporary ceasefire between Pakistan and a local Pakistani Taliban group after talks in Kabul.
evidence.title: Afghanistan's Taliban mediate ceasefire between Pakistan, local militants
evidence.excerpt: The Taliban in Afghanistan mediated a temporary ceasefire between Pakistan and a local Pakistani Taliban group after talks in Kabul.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a live diplomatic/security process with direct attribution from Taliban and TTP statements.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Pakistan side at the government/security level, but Reuters says it was not clear who represented Pakistan in the talks.
contrary_evidence: The ceasefire was temporary, and the reporting does not identify a clear PM-level negotiator.

evidence.claim: A major border crossing closed after prolonged firing between security forces from both sides, with the Taliban describing the incident as a misunderstanding.
evidence.title: Pakistan-Afghan border crossing closed after clashes
evidence.excerpt: A major border crossing closed after prolonged firing between security forces from both sides, with the Taliban describing the incident as a misunderstanding.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting provides a clear contemporaneous account of the clash and closure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Border-management crisis under Sharif, but responsibility for initiating the clash was disputed.
contrary_evidence: Both sides blamed each other and the Taliban said it was a misunderstanding, so initiation is not cleanly attributable.

evidence.claim: Pakistan said six Pakistani nationals were killed and 17 wounded after Afghan border forces fired on civilians in Chaman, and urged strict action to avoid recurrence.
evidence.title: Press Release
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan said six Pakistani nationals were killed and 17 wounded after Afghan border forces fired on civilians in Chaman, and urged strict action to avoid recurrence.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official statement with specific casualty and de-escalation language, but the underlying incident account is contested by the Afghan side.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government response under Sharif; not a personal order or battlefield decision by the PM.
contrary_evidence: Afghan authorities likely had a different account of the incident, so the casualty and responsibility framing is contested.

evidence.claim: Pakistan condemned cross-border shelling in Chaman-Spin Boldak, said civilian protection was a shared responsibility, and said peace along the border was intrinsic to fraternal relations.
evidence.title: Afghan Chargé d’Affaires called to the Foreign Ministry over Chaman Incident
evidence.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
evidence.excerpt: Pakistan condemned cross-border shelling in Chaman-Spin Boldak, said civilian protection was a shared responsibility, and said peace along the border was intrinsic to fraternal relations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated official statement with direct de-escalatory language and explicit border-peace framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Official government response under Sharif, though still not a direct PM operational order.
contrary_evidence: This statement does not settle who initiated the incident or whether later steps reduced the underlying border risk.
